title: introduce-stateful-rag-finite-state-machine-quickstart
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a new quickstart demonstrating a finite-state-machine-driven RAG orchestration for stateful sessions, includes authoring guide, example code, and lightweight smoke CI.
description: Context & motivation: Many teams want RAG flows that maintain explicit conversational state across turns (session phases, latent tool state, multi-step confirmations) without shipping a heavyweight orchestrator. This PR introduces a compact Quickstart that wires a finite-state-machine (FSM) pattern to Redwood's tool-calling and incremental index APIs so developers can bootstrap stateful RAG sessions with clear guardrails and reproducible telemetry. Summary of changes: 1) new quickstart: quickstarts/stateful-fsm-rag/ containing a README, TypeScript sample runner, an auth-free local dev shim, and a test harness; 2) authoring doc: docs/authoring/stateful-rag-fsm.md with design rationale and recommended prompt templates; 3) telemetry presets: quickstarts/stateful-fsm-rag/telemetry-presets.json for Console probe ingestion; 4) smoke CI workflow: .github/workflows/qst-stateful-fsm-smoke.yml to validate local run in CI; 5) small SDK helper: packages/sdk-utils/src/fsm.ts (new lightweight FSM utilities) 6) tests: quickstarts/stateful-fsm-rag/__tests__/fsm-smoke.test.ts High-level commit summary: - Initial quickstart scaffold and README. - Add FSM runtime helpers and inline JSDoc + types. - Add authoring guide with example prompts and guardrails. - Add telemetry presets and console link example. - Add GitHub smoke workflow and a minimal unit test. Changed areas/files (high level): quickstarts/stateful-fsm-rag/{README.md,runner.ts,telemetry-presets.json,__tests__/fsm-smoke.test.ts}, docs/authoring/stateful-rag-fsm.md, packages/sdk-utils/src/fsm.ts, .github/workflows/qst-stateful-fsm-smoke.yml Notable design points: - FSM model: explicit states (INIT, RETRIEVE, TOOL_CALL, CONFIRM, FINALIZE) and deterministic transitions on structured outputs. - Tool binding: demonstrates idempotent tool wrappers and a replay-safe invocation pattern using request-scoped tokens. - Caching: shows prefix KV caching for retrieval tokens between RETRIEVE->TOOL_CALL transitions to reduce repeated embedding calls. - Telemetry: emits per-state timers and transition tags consumed by Redwood Console via provided presets. Single-line summary of example runner behavior: The TS runner seeds an in-memory index, starts a session in INIT, emits a retrieval request, enters RETRIEVE, chooses candidate passages, optionally enters TOOL_CALL (e.g., call external knowledge API or custom search tool), moves to CONFIRM when candidate requires human-in-loop confirmation, and then FINALIZE to return structured output; the runner includes a --simulate-human flag for deterministic CI. Review conversation (high-level): Diego: "Please add an example of error path transition when retrieval returns empty; show fallback to open-domain generation." Author (Maya): "Added fallback transition with explicit prompt template and covered in authoring doc." Priya: "Telemetry presets look good; please ensure tags use kebab-case." Author: "Fixed tags and added unit test asserting telemetry fields." Samir (approval): "Works for me, tests and CI pass." CI checks: lint (pass), unit-tests (pass), smoke-ci-run (pass after one rerun for environment flakiness), docs-build (pass). Testing notes: smoke CI uses node 18 and a lightweight in-memory vector index, tests assert deterministic outputs using seeded RNG. Migration/compat notes: SDK helper fsm.ts is additive and exported from packages/sdk-utils index without breaking existing APIs. Rollout plan: ship as a Quickstart under the Quickstarts landing page with a short blurb and a linked authoring guide. Merge outcome: merged via squash-merge after approvals. How to review locally: 1) cd quickstarts/stateful-fsm-rag 2) yarn install && yarn build 3) yarn run seed && yarn run start -- --simulate-human 4) run the smoke test: yarn test:fsm-smoke Why this is different from other RAG quickstarts: most quickstarts focus on tool-calling, debugging, or replay; this one centers an explicit FSM pattern and shows best practices for state transitions, telemetry tags per state, idempotent tool wrappers, and KV-backed retrieval caching. Related linear/Jira: ENG-2103 (FSM runtime utility), PM-812 (Quickstart deliverable).
